1.explanation: The root of the violation is in FileUploaderButton.render: it declares a static role="button" on the <label> but then also spreads a dynamic role={role} from props (via {...other}), which can override or inject an empty/invalid ARIA role into the DOM. This produces the DAP error because the resulting role attribute isn’t guaranteed to be a valid WAI-ARIA role. Removing the dynamic role prop (and any role PropType) from the label element ensures that only the intended, valid role="button" is present and clears the accessibility violation.
1.bug_scenario: When running DAP against a page containing the FileUploaderButton component, the audit flags the <label> element as an invalid ARIA role because it’s being rendered with a dynamic role prop that may be empty or invalid. In the screenshot you can see the DOM node for the button label (<label role= tabindex=…) is flagged with “Elements that use 'role' must reference a valid WAI-ARIA role.” The report even notes “To fix this issue remove ‘role’ from the label.”

2.explanation: The FileUploaderButton class is the component that renders the offending <label>. Inside its render() method you see two "role" props on the label (one hard-coded and one passed in), which is what triggers the accessibility violation. Removing the role attribute from the <label> in FileUploaderButton.render (and removing the corresponding propType definition) will fix the invalid-role DAP error.
2.bug_scenario: When you render the FileUploaderButton component, its root <label> element is being given a "role" attribute (in this case "button") which is not a valid ARIA role for a <label>. The attached DevTools screenshot shows the DAP panel flagging “Elements that use 'role' must reference a valid WAI-ARIA role,” pointing at the <label role="button">. To eliminate the violation, the hard-coded "role" on the label must be removed (and the propType for it deprecated or deleted).
